name: Mountain Pose (Tadasana)
instructions: Stand with feet together, arms at your sides.
Distribute your weight evenly across both feet.
Engage your thighs and lift your kneecaps without locking the knees.
Lengthen your tailbone toward the floor and lift the crown of your head toward the ceiling.
Roll your shoulders back and down, and let your arms hang naturally with palms facing forward.
Hold for 5-10 breaths, maintaining steady breathing.

name: Warrior I (Virabhadrasana I)
instructions: From Mountain Pose, step your left foot back 3-4 feet.
Turn your left foot out about 45 degrees, keeping your right foot pointing forward.
Bend your right knee to 90 degrees, stacking it over the ankle.
Square your hips toward the front of the mat.
Raise both arms overhead with palms facing each other.
Hold for 5-8 breaths, then switch sides.

name: Warrior II (Virabhadrasana II)
instructions: From standing, step your feet wide apart, about 4 feet.
Turn your right foot out 90 degrees and your left foot slightly inward.
Extend your arms out to the sides at shoulder height, palms facing down.
Bend your right knee to 90 degrees, keeping it aligned over the ankle.
Gaze over your right fingertips and sink your hips low.
Hold for 5-8 breaths, then switch sides.

name: Warrior III (Virabhadrasana III)
instructions: From Warrior I, shift your weight onto your front foot.
Hinge forward at the hips, lifting your back leg off the ground.
Extend your arms forward alongside your ears or alongside your body.
Create a straight line from fingertips to back foot, parallel to the floor.
Keep your standing leg strong with a micro-bend in the knee.
Hold for 5-8 breaths, then switch sides.

name: Triangle Pose (Trikonasana)
instructions: Stand with your feet wide apart, about 4 feet.
Turn your right foot out 90 degrees and your left foot slightly inward.
Extend your arms to the sides at shoulder height.
Reach your right hand toward your right foot, hinging at the hip.
Place your right hand on your shin, ankle, or the floor, and extend your left arm straight up.
Gaze up at your left hand. Hold for 5-8 breaths, then switch sides.

name: Extended Side Angle (Utthita Parsvakonasana)
instructions: From Warrior II, lower your right forearm to your right thigh or place your right hand on the floor outside your right foot.
Extend your left arm overhead, creating a long line from your left heel to your left fingertips.
Keep your chest open, rotating your torso toward the ceiling.
Engage your core and press firmly through both feet.
Hold for 5-8 breaths, then switch sides.

name: Half Moon Pose (Ardha Chandrasana)
instructions: From Triangle Pose on the right side, bend your right knee and shift your weight onto your right foot.
Place your right hand on the floor about 12 inches in front of your right foot.
Lift your left leg parallel to the floor.
Open your left hip, stacking it over the right, and extend your left arm upward.
Flex your lifted foot and gaze up at your left hand.
Hold for 5-8 breaths, then switch sides.

name: Tree Pose (Vrksasana)
instructions: Stand in Mountain Pose and shift your weight onto your left foot.
Place the sole of your right foot on your left inner thigh or calf (avoid the knee).
Press your foot and leg into each other for stability.
Bring your hands to heart center or extend them overhead.
Fix your gaze on a steady point for balance.
Hold for 5-10 breaths, then switch sides.

name: Chair Pose (Utkatasana)
instructions: Stand with feet together in Mountain Pose.
Bend your knees deeply as if sitting into an imaginary chair.
Keep your weight in your heels and your knees behind your toes.
Extend your arms overhead alongside your ears, palms facing each other.
Engage your core and lengthen your tailbone toward the floor.
Hold for 5-8 breaths.

name: Eagle Pose (Garudasana)
instructions: Stand in Mountain Pose and bend your knees slightly.
Cross your right thigh over your left, hooking your right foot behind your left calf if possible.
Extend your arms forward, cross your left arm over the right, and bend at the elbows.
Wrap your forearms and press your palms together.
Sink your hips low and lift your elbows to shoulder height.
Hold for 5-8 breaths, then switch sides.

name: Dancer Pose (Natarajasana)
instructions: Stand in Mountain Pose and shift your weight onto your left foot.
Bend your right knee and grasp the inside of your right ankle with your right hand.
Extend your left arm forward and up.
Press your right foot into your hand, lifting the leg behind you.
Hinge slightly forward, keeping your chest lifted.
Hold for 5-8 breaths, then switch sides.

name: Standing Forward Fold (Uttanasana)
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart in Mountain Pose.
Hinge forward at your hips, leading with your chest.
Let your hands reach toward the floor, your shins, or grasp your elbows.
Relax your head and neck, letting them hang heavy.
Keep a slight bend in your knees if your hamstrings are tight.
Hold for 5-10 breaths.

name: Wide-Legged Forward Fold (Prasarita Padottanasana)
instructions: Stand with your feet 4-5 feet apart, toes pointing slightly inward.
Place your hands on your hips and hinge forward at the hips.
Place your hands on the floor between your feet.
Walk your hands back in line with your feet if flexibility allows.
Let the crown of your head drop toward the floor.
Hold for 5-10 breaths.

name: Pyramid Pose (Parsvottanasana)
instructions: From Mountain Pose, step your left foot back about 3 feet.
Square your hips toward the front of the mat.
Bring your hands behind your back in reverse prayer or hold opposite elbows.
Hinge forward over your right leg, keeping your spine long.
Fold as deeply as comfortable while keeping both legs straight.
Hold for 5-8 breaths, then switch sides.

name: Revolved Triangle (Parivrtta Trikonasana)
instructions: From Pyramid Pose on the right side, place your left hand on the floor or a block outside your right foot.
Twist your torso to the right, extending your right arm toward the ceiling.
Keep both hips squared toward the front.
Stack your shoulders and gaze up at your top hand.
Engage your core to support the twist.
Hold for 5-8 breaths, then switch sides.

name: High Lunge (Utthita Ashwa Sanchalanasana)
instructions: From Standing Forward Fold, step your left foot back into a lunge position.
Keep your right knee bent at 90 degrees, aligned over the ankle.
Stay on the ball of your back foot with your heel lifted.
Raise your arms overhead, framing your ears.
Engage your core and keep your hips squared forward.
Hold for 5-8 breaths, then switch sides.

name: Crescent Lunge (Anjaneyasana)
instructions: From a low lunge, lower your back knee to the floor.
Slide your back leg further behind you to deepen the hip flexor stretch.
Sweep your arms overhead and gently arch your back.
Keep your front knee stacked over the ankle.
Lift your chest and gaze upward.
Hold for 5-8 breaths, then switch sides.

name: Standing Split (Urdhva Prasarita Eka Padasana)
instructions: From Standing Forward Fold, shift your weight onto your left foot.
Lift your right leg straight up behind you as high as possible.
Keep your hips squared toward the floor.
Walk your hands closer to your standing foot for a deeper stretch.
Keep your standing leg strong with a micro-bend in the knee.
Hold for 5-8 breaths, then switch sides.

name: Goddess Pose (Utkata Konasana)
instructions: Stand with feet wide apart, about 4 feet, toes turned out 45 degrees.
Bend your knees deeply, sinking your hips to knee height.
Keep your knees tracking over your toes.
Bring your arms to goal-post position or cactus arms at shoulder height.
Engage your core and keep your spine tall.
Hold for 5-8 breaths.

name: Garland Pose (Malasana)
instructions: Stand with feet slightly wider than hip-width, toes turned out.
Squat deeply, lowering your hips toward the floor.
Bring your palms together at heart center.
Press your elbows against your inner knees to open your hips.
Keep your spine long and chest lifted.
Hold for 5-10 breaths.

name: Standing Hand-to-Big-Toe (Utthita Hasta Padangusthasana)
instructions: Stand in Mountain Pose and shift your weight onto your left foot.
Lift your right knee toward your chest and grab your right big toe with your right hand.
Slowly extend your right leg forward, straightening it as much as possible.
Keep your standing leg strong and your spine upright.
Optionally open your right leg out to the side.
Hold for 5-8 breaths, then switch sides.

name: Seated Forward Fold (Paschimottanasana)
instructions: Sit on the floor with legs extended straight in front of you.
Flex your feet and sit tall, lengthening your spine.
Inhale and reach your arms overhead.
Exhale and hinge forward from the hips, reaching for your feet or shins.
Keep your spine long rather than rounding your back.
Hold for 5-10 breaths, deepening the fold with each exhale.

name: Head-to-Knee Pose (Janu Sirsasana)
instructions: Sit with both legs extended. Bend your right knee and place the sole of your right foot against your left inner thigh.
Turn your torso to face your extended left leg.
Inhale and lengthen your spine upward.
Exhale and fold forward over your left leg, reaching for your foot.
Keep your left foot flexed and leg active.
Hold for 5-8 breaths, then switch sides.

name: Butterfly Pose (Baddha Konasana)
instructions: Sit on the floor and bring the soles of your feet together, letting your knees fall open.
Hold your feet or ankles with your hands.
Sit up tall, lengthening your spine.
Gently press your knees toward the floor using your elbows.
For a deeper stretch, fold forward from the hips.
Hold for 5-10 breaths.

name: Half Lord of the Fishes (Ardha Matsyendrasana)
instructions: Sit with legs extended. Bend your right knee and place your right foot outside your left thigh.
Bend your left knee and tuck your left foot near your right hip.
Place your right hand behind you for support.
Hook your left elbow outside your right knee.
Inhale to lengthen your spine, exhale to deepen the twist.
Hold for 5-8 breaths, then switch sides.

name: Lotus Pose (Padmasana)
instructions: Sit with legs extended in Staff Pose.
Bend your right knee and place your right foot on top of your left thigh, close to the hip crease.
Bend your left knee and place your left foot on top of your right thigh.
Press your knees gently toward the floor.
Rest your hands on your knees in a mudra or place them palms-up.
Sit tall with a long spine. Hold for several minutes with steady breathing.

name: Hero Pose (Virasana)
instructions: Kneel on the floor with your knees together and feet slightly wider than hip-width.
Sit back between your feet, using a block or cushion if needed.
Place the tops of your feet on the floor with toes pointing straight back.
Rest your hands on your thighs.
Lengthen your spine and lift through the crown of your head.
Hold for 1-3 minutes.

name: Staff Pose (Dandasana)
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs extended straight in front of you.
Flex your feet and press through your heels.
Place your palms on the floor beside your hips, fingers pointing forward.
Sit up tall, stacking your shoulders over your hips.
Engage your core and quadriceps.
Hold for 5-10 breaths.

name: Cow Face Pose (Gomukhasana)
instructions: Sit and stack your right knee on top of your left, aligning both knees at center.
Bring your feet toward opposite hips.
Reach your right arm overhead, bend the elbow, and drop your right hand behind your back.
Reach your left arm behind your back from below and clasp your hands together.
Use a strap between hands if they do not reach.
Hold for 5-8 breaths, then switch sides.

name: Fire Log Pose (Agnistambhasana)
instructions: Sit on the floor and stack your right shin on top of your left shin.
Align your right ankle over your left knee and your right knee over your left ankle.
Flex both feet to protect the knees.
Sit tall and lengthen your spine.
For a deeper stretch, hinge forward from the hips.
Hold for 5-8 breaths, then switch the stacking.

name: Boat Pose (Navasana)
instructions: Sit with knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Lean back slightly, lifting your feet off the floor.
Straighten your legs to form a V-shape with your torso.
Extend your arms forward, parallel to the floor.
Keep your chest lifted and core engaged.
Hold for 5-10 breaths.

name: Pigeon Pose (Eka Pada Rajakapotasana)
instructions: From Downward Dog, bring your right knee forward toward your right wrist.
Angle your right shin so your foot is near your left hip (or more parallel to the front of the mat for more intensity).
Extend your left leg straight behind you, top of the foot on the floor.
Square your hips toward the front of the mat.
Walk your hands forward and lower your torso over your front shin.
Hold for 5-10 breaths, then switch sides.

name: Seated Wide-Angle Forward Fold (Upavistha Konasana)
instructions: Sit on the floor and open your legs wide into a straddle position.
Flex your feet and keep your kneecaps pointing toward the ceiling.
Sit tall and lengthen your spine.
Walk your hands forward between your legs, folding from the hips.
Keep your spine long as you fold deeper.
Hold for 5-10 breaths.

name: Easy Pose (Sukhasana)
instructions: Sit on the floor and cross your shins, placing each foot beneath the opposite knee.
Rest your hands on your knees, palms up or down.
Sit tall, lengthening from your tailbone to the crown of your head.
Relax your shoulders down and back.
Close your eyes and breathe deeply.
Hold for 1-5 minutes, switching the cross of your legs halfway through.

name: Cobra Pose (Bhujangasana)
instructions: Lie face down with your legs extended and the tops of your feet on the floor.
Place your hands under your shoulders, elbows close to your body.
Press into your hands and slowly lift your chest off the floor.
Keep your elbows slightly bent and shoulders away from your ears.
Engage your back muscles; do not rely solely on your arms.
Hold for 5-8 breaths.

name: Upward-Facing Dog (Urdhva Mukha Svanasana)
instructions: Lie face down and place your hands beside your lower ribs.
Press into your hands, straightening your arms and lifting your torso and thighs off the floor.
Only the tops of your feet and your palms should touch the floor.
Roll your shoulders back and lift your chest high.
Keep your legs engaged and kneecaps lifted.
Hold for 3-5 breaths.

name: Locust Pose (Salabhasana)
instructions: Lie face down with arms alongside your body, palms facing up.
Rest your forehead on the floor.
On an inhale, lift your head, chest, arms, and legs off the floor simultaneously.
Reach your arms back toward your feet and extend through your toes.
Keep your gaze slightly forward and neck in a neutral position.
Hold for 5-8 breaths.

name: Bow Pose (Dhanurasana)
instructions: Lie face down and bend your knees, bringing your heels toward your glutes.
Reach back and grasp your ankles with your hands.
On an inhale, press your feet into your hands, lifting your chest and thighs off the floor.
Keep your knees hip-width apart.
Look forward and breathe deeply into your chest.
Hold for 5-8 breaths.

name: Sphinx Pose (Salamba Bhujangasana)
instructions: Lie face down with your legs extended behind you.
Place your forearms on the floor with elbows directly under your shoulders.
Press into your forearms and lift your chest off the floor.
Keep your lower body relaxed and grounded.
Draw your shoulder blades together and down.
Hold for 5-10 breaths.

name: Downward-Facing Dog (Adho Mukha Svanasana)
instructions: Start on your hands and knees in a tabletop position.
Tuck your toes and lift your hips up and back.
Straighten your legs as much as possible, pressing your heels toward the floor.
Spread your fingers wide and press firmly through your palms.
Create an inverted V-shape, keeping your spine long.
Hold for 5-10 breaths.

name: Plank Pose (Phalakasana)
instructions: Start in a tabletop position with wrists under shoulders.
Step your feet back one at a time, extending your legs fully.
Create a straight line from your head to your heels.
Engage your core and squeeze your glutes.
Keep your gaze slightly forward, neck neutral.
Hold for 5-10 breaths or 30-60 seconds.

name: Bridge Pose (Setu Bandhasana)
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet hip-width apart, close to your glutes.
Press into your feet and lift your hips toward the ceiling.
Interlace your fingers under your back and walk your shoulders closer together.
Keep your thighs parallel and knees over your ankles.
Lift your chest toward your chin.
Hold for 5-10 breaths.

name: Wheel Pose (Urdhva Dhanurasana)
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat on the floor hip-width apart.
Place your hands beside your ears with fingers pointing toward your shoulders.
Press into your hands and feet, lifting your hips and shoulders off the floor.
Straighten your arms as much as possible, pressing your chest forward.
Keep your feet parallel and engage your legs.
Hold for 5-8 breaths.

name: Fish Pose (Matsyasana)
instructions: Lie on your back with legs extended and arms alongside your body.
Slide your hands under your hips, palms facing down.
Press into your forearms and elbows, lifting your chest toward the ceiling.
Drop the crown of your head back to lightly touch the floor.
Keep most of the weight on your forearms, not your head.
Hold for 5-8 breaths.

name: Happy Baby Pose (Ananda Balasana)
instructions: Lie on your back and draw your knees toward your chest.
Grab the outsides of your feet with your hands.
Open your knees wider than your torso and pull them toward your armpits.
Keep your ankles directly over your knees, shins perpendicular to the floor.
Gently rock side to side to massage your lower back.
Hold for 5-10 breaths.

name: Supine Spinal Twist (Supta Matsyendrasana)
instructions: Lie on your back and draw your right knee toward your chest.
Guide your right knee across your body to the left, using your left hand.
Extend your right arm out to the side at shoulder height.
Turn your head to gaze toward your right hand.
Let gravity deepen the twist; keep both shoulders on the floor.
Hold for 5-10 breaths, then switch sides.

name: Legs Up the Wall (Viparita Karani)
instructions: Sit sideways next to a wall, then swing your legs up as you lie back.
Scoot your hips as close to the wall as comfortable.
Rest your legs vertically against the wall.
Place your arms at your sides, palms up.
Close your eyes and relax completely.
Hold for 5-15 minutes.

name: Wind-Relieving Pose (Pavanamuktasana)
instructions: Lie on your back with both legs extended.
Draw your right knee toward your chest and interlace your fingers around your shin.
Keep your left leg extended on the floor or bent with foot flat.
Gently pull your knee closer to your chest.
Keep your head and shoulders relaxed on the floor.
Hold for 5-8 breaths, then switch sides. Repeat with both knees.

name: Reclined Hand-to-Big-Toe (Supta Padangusthasana)
instructions: Lie on your back with both legs extended.
Draw your right knee toward your chest and loop a strap or grab your big toe.
Extend your right leg toward the ceiling, straightening it as much as possible.
Keep your left leg active and pressed into the floor.
Relax your shoulders and keep your hips level.
Hold for 5-8 breaths, then switch sides.

name: Headstand (Sirsasana)
instructions: Kneel and interlace your fingers, placing your forearms on the floor with elbows shoulder-width apart.
Place the crown of your head on the floor, cradled by your interlaced hands.
Tuck your toes and lift your hips, walking your feet toward your head.
Engage your core and slowly lift both legs overhead until your body is inverted.
Stack your hips over your shoulders and your ankles over your hips.
Hold for 5-20 breaths, coming down slowly and resting in Child's Pose.

name: Shoulderstand (Sarvangasana)
instructions: Lie on your back with arms at your sides.
Lift your legs and hips off the floor, bringing your legs overhead.
Place your hands on your lower back for support, elbows on the floor.
Straighten your legs toward the ceiling, stacking hips over shoulders.
Keep your weight on your shoulders and upper arms, not your neck.
Hold for 10-25 breaths.

name: Plow Pose (Halasana)
instructions: From Shoulderstand, slowly lower your legs over your head.
Bring your toes to touch the floor behind your head.
Keep your legs straight and engage your thighs.
Interlace your fingers on the floor and walk your shoulders under you.
Keep your neck neutral and avoid turning your head.
Hold for 5-10 breaths.

name: Forearm Stand (Pincha Mayurasana)
instructions: Start in Dolphin Pose with forearms on the floor, shoulder-width apart.
Walk your feet toward your elbows, lifting your hips high.
Gaze between your forearms and engage your core.
Kick one leg up and then the other, finding balance upside down.
Stack your hips over your shoulders and legs over your hips.
Hold for 5-10 breaths, using a wall for support if needed.

name: Handstand (Adho Mukha Vrksasana)
instructions: Stand facing a wall about one foot away.
Place your hands shoulder-width apart on the floor, fingers spread wide.
Kick one leg up and then the other, using the wall for support.
Stack your body in a straight vertical line from wrists to ankles.
Engage your core, squeeze your legs together, and point your toes.
Hold for 5-15 breaths, building up duration over time.

name: Dolphin Pose (Ardha Pincha Mayurasana)
instructions: Start on hands and knees, then lower to your forearms.
Tuck your toes and lift your hips up and back, like Downward Dog on forearms.
Keep your forearms parallel and press firmly into the floor.
Walk your feet closer to your elbows to increase the shoulder stretch.
Keep your head off the floor and gaze toward your feet.
Hold for 5-10 breaths.

name: Supported Headstand (Salamba Sirsasana II)
instructions: Place the crown of your head on the floor and your palms flat on either side, fingers pointing forward.
Walk your feet in toward your head, lifting your hips over your shoulders.
Engage your core and slowly lift your legs to vertical.
Press firmly through your hands to take weight off your neck.
Find balance by stacking your entire body in one line.
Hold for 5-15 breaths.

name: Ragdoll Pose (Uttanasana Variation)
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart and fold forward from the hips.
Bend your knees generously and grab opposite elbows with your hands.
Let your head hang heavy, releasing tension in the neck.
Gently sway side to side to release the lower back.
Keep your weight slightly forward toward the balls of your feet.
Hold for 5-10 breaths.

name: Crow Pose (Bakasana)
instructions: Squat down and place your hands shoulder-width apart on the floor.
Spread your fingers wide and bend your elbows slightly.
Place your knees on the backs of your upper arms, near your armpits.
Lean forward, shifting your weight into your hands.
Slowly lift one foot, then the other, off the floor.
Hold for 5-10 breaths, gazing slightly forward.

name: Side Crow (Parsva Bakasana)
instructions: Squat and twist your torso to the right, placing both hands on the floor to your right.
Hook your left hip or outer thigh onto your right upper arm.
Lean forward and shift your weight into your hands.
Lift both feet off the floor, stacking your legs.
Engage your core to maintain the twist and balance.
Hold for 5-8 breaths, then switch sides.

name: Firefly Pose (Tittibhasana)
instructions: Squat with feet slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Tilt forward and thread your arms between and behind your legs.
Place your palms flat on the floor behind your feet.
Shift your weight into your hands and lift your feet off the floor.
Straighten your legs out to the sides, extending through your heels.
Hold for 5-8 breaths.

name: Eight-Angle Pose (Astavakrasana)
instructions: Sit and hook your right leg over your right upper arm, high on the shoulder.
Cross your left ankle over your right and squeeze your legs together.
Place both hands on the floor and shift your weight forward.
Bend your elbows like Chaturanga and extend your legs to the right.
Keep your core strongly engaged and gaze forward.
Hold for 5-8 breaths, then switch sides.

name: Peacock Pose (Mayurasana)
instructions: Kneel and place your hands on the floor with fingers pointing toward your body.
Bend your elbows and press them into your abdomen.
Lean forward, placing your forehead on the floor.
Straighten your legs behind you and engage your core.
Shift your weight forward until your feet and head lift off the floor.
Hold for 3-8 breaths.

name: Scale Pose (Tolasana)
instructions: Sit in Lotus Pose (or cross-legged if Lotus is not accessible).
Place your palms on the floor beside your hips.
Press firmly into your hands and lift your entire body off the floor.
Engage your core and hip flexors to lift your crossed legs.
Keep your shoulders down and away from your ears.
Hold for 5-10 breaths.

name: Flying Pigeon (Eka Pada Galavasana)
instructions: From standing, cross your right ankle over your left knee in a figure-four.
Bend your standing leg and fold forward, placing your hands on the floor.
Hook your right foot around your left upper arm.
Lean forward, bend your elbows, and shift your weight into your hands.
Extend your left leg straight back as you lift off.
Hold for 5-8 breaths, then switch sides.

name: Side Plank Pose (Vasisthasana)
instructions: From Plank Pose, shift your weight onto your right hand and the outer edge of your right foot.
Stack your left foot on top of your right.
Extend your left arm toward the ceiling.
Keep your body in one straight line from head to heels.
Engage your core and lift your hips.
Hold for 5-8 breaths, then switch sides.

name: Four-Limbed Staff Pose (Chaturanga Dandasana)
instructions: From Plank Pose, shift slightly forward on your toes.
Bend your elbows straight back, lowering your body halfway to the floor.
Keep your elbows hugged close to your ribs at 90 degrees.
Maintain a straight line from head to heels.
Engage your core and keep your shoulders above elbow height.
Hold for 1-3 breaths before pressing up or transitioning.

name: Flying Crow (Eka Pada Bakasana)
instructions: Start in Crow Pose with knees on the backs of your arms.
Slowly extend one leg straight back, keeping the other knee on your arm.
Engage your core strongly to maintain balance.
Gaze slightly forward, keeping your weight centered over your hands.
Keep your extended leg active and parallel to the floor.
Hold for 3-5 breaths, then switch legs.

name: Revolved Chair Pose (Parivrtta Utkatasana)
instructions: Start in Chair Pose with feet together and knees bent.
Bring your palms together at heart center.
Twist to the right, hooking your left elbow outside your right knee.
Press your palms together to deepen the twist.
Keep your knees aligned and hips level.
Hold for 5-8 breaths, then switch sides.

name: Revolved Crescent Lunge (Parivrtta Anjaneyasana)
instructions: From High Lunge with your right foot forward, bring your palms to heart center.
Twist to the right, hooking your left elbow outside your right knee.
Press your palms together and use the leverage to deepen the twist.
Keep your back leg strong and your heel lifted.
Open your chest toward the ceiling.
Hold for 5-8 breaths, then switch sides.

name: Revolved Side Angle (Parivrtta Parsvakonasana)
instructions: From a High Lunge with your right foot forward, twist to the right.
Place your left hand on the floor outside your right foot (or on a block).
Extend your right arm overhead, creating a line from your back heel to your fingertips.
Open your chest toward the ceiling.
Keep your front knee at 90 degrees and your back leg strong.
Hold for 5-8 breaths, then switch sides.

name: Simple Seated Twist (Parivrtta Sukhasana)
instructions: Sit in Easy Pose with a tall spine.
Place your left hand on your right knee.
Place your right hand behind you on the floor.
Inhale to lengthen your spine, exhale to twist to the right.
Keep both sitting bones grounded.
Hold for 5-8 breaths, then switch sides.

name: Revolved Head-to-Knee (Parivrtta Janu Sirsasana)
instructions: Sit with legs in a wide straddle. Bend your right knee, placing the sole of your foot against your left inner thigh.
Lean your torso to the left toward your extended leg.
Reach your left hand toward your left foot and your right arm overhead.
Rotate your chest toward the ceiling.
Keep your left leg active with the foot flexed.
Hold for 5-8 breaths, then switch sides.

name: Bharadvaja's Twist (Bharadvajasana)
instructions: Sit with legs extended, then shift both legs to the left so your feet are beside your left hip.
Place your left hand on your right knee.
Place your right hand behind you on the floor.
Inhale to lengthen your spine, exhale to twist to the right.
Look over your right shoulder.
Hold for 5-8 breaths, then switch sides.

name: Twisted Lizard Pose (Parivrtta Utthan Pristhasana)
instructions: From a low lunge with your right foot forward, place both hands inside your right foot.
Lower your back knee to the floor.
Reach your right hand back to grab your left foot.
Twist your torso open to the right.
Use the foot-to-hand connection to deepen the quad stretch and twist.
Hold for 5-8 breaths, then switch sides.

name: Noose Pose (Pasasana)
instructions: Squat with your feet together, heels on the floor (use a blanket if needed).
Twist your torso to the right, wrapping your left arm around the outside of your right thigh.
Reach your right arm behind your back and bind your hands together.
Keep your knees together and chest lifted.
Deepen the twist with each exhale.
Hold for 5-8 breaths, then switch sides.

name: Child's Pose (Balasana)
instructions: Kneel on the floor with your big toes touching and knees wide apart.
Sit back on your heels.
Fold forward, extending your arms in front of you on the floor.
Rest your forehead on the mat.
Let your entire body relax and soften.
Hold for 1-3 minutes, breathing deeply.

name: Reclined Bound Angle Pose (Supta Baddha Konasana)
instructions: Lie on your back and bring the soles of your feet together.
Let your knees fall open to the sides.
Place your arms at your sides, palms facing up.
Support your knees with blocks or pillows if needed.
Close your eyes and breathe deeply into your belly.
Hold for 3-10 minutes.

name: Supported Fish Pose (Salamba Matsyasana)
instructions: Place a bolster or rolled blanket lengthwise on the floor.
Sit in front of the bolster and lie back so it supports your spine from mid-back to head.
Let your arms rest open at your sides, palms facing up.
Extend your legs or bring the soles of your feet together.
Allow your chest to open and your shoulders to release.
Hold for 3-10 minutes.

name: Corpse Pose (Savasana)
instructions: Lie flat on your back with legs extended and arms at your sides.
Let your feet fall open and turn your palms to face the ceiling.
Close your eyes and release all muscular effort.
Scan your body from head to toe, consciously relaxing each area.
Focus on your natural breath without trying to control it.
Remain still for 5-15 minutes.

name: Supported Bridge Pose (Salamba Setu Bandhasana)
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Lift your hips and place a block or bolster under your sacrum.
Rest your weight on the support, allowing your back to release.
Extend your arms at your sides or overhead.
Optionally extend your legs one at a time for a deeper stretch.
Hold for 3-10 minutes.

name: Restorative Supine Twist (Supta Matsyendrasana Variation)
instructions: Lie on your back and draw both knees to your chest.
Let both knees fall to the right side, resting on a bolster or pillow.
Extend your arms out to the sides in a T-shape.
Turn your head to the left if comfortable.
Allow gravity to deepen the twist without forcing.
Hold for 3-5 minutes, then switch sides.

name: Supported Child's Pose (Salamba Balasana)
instructions: Place a bolster lengthwise on your mat.
Kneel with knees wide and sit back on your heels.
Fold forward over the bolster, turning your head to one side.
Let your arms drape along the sides of the bolster.
Allow your entire body to relax into the support.
Hold for 3-10 minutes, switching the direction of your head halfway.

name: Constructive Rest Pose
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart.
Let your knees rest against each other so your legs can fully relax.
Place your hands on your belly or at your sides.
Close your eyes and allow your lower back to release into the floor.
Breathe naturally and let go of all tension.
Hold for 5-15 minutes.

name: Thread the Needle Pose (Parsva Balasana)
instructions: Start in a tabletop position on hands and knees.
Slide your right arm underneath your left arm, lowering your right shoulder and temple to the floor.
Keep your left hand planted or extend it forward for a deeper stretch.
Keep your hips stacked over your knees.
Feel the stretch across your right shoulder and upper back.
Hold for 5-8 breaths, then switch sides.

name: Cat Pose (Marjaryasana)
instructions: Start in a tabletop position with wrists under shoulders and knees under hips.
On an exhale, round your spine toward the ceiling.
Tuck your tailbone and draw your chin toward your chest.
Press the floor away with your hands to maximize the stretch.
Engage your abdominals to support the rounding.
Alternate with Cow Pose for 5-10 rounds.

name: Cow Pose (Bitilasana)
instructions: Start in a tabletop position with wrists under shoulders and knees under hips.
On an inhale, drop your belly toward the floor.
Lift your chest and tailbone toward the ceiling.
Gaze forward or slightly upward.
Broaden across your collarbones.
Alternate with Cat Pose for 5-10 rounds.

name: Camel Pose (Ustrasana)
instructions: Kneel with your knees hip-width apart, thighs perpendicular to the floor.
Place your hands on your lower back, fingers pointing down.
Engage your core and begin to arch backward.
Reach your hands back to grasp your heels (or keep them on your lower back).
Push your hips forward and lift your chest toward the ceiling.
Hold for 5-8 breaths.

name: Gate Pose (Parighasana)
instructions: Kneel on the floor and extend your right leg out to the side, foot flat on the floor.
Inhale and reach your left arm overhead.
Exhale and lean to the right, sliding your right hand down your right leg.
Create a long stretch along your left side body.
Keep your chest open, not collapsing forward.
Hold for 5-8 breaths, then switch sides.

name: Wild Thing (Camatkarasana)
instructions: From Downward Dog, lift your right leg and open your hip.
Let your right foot drop behind you, spinning onto the ball of your right foot.
Lift your right hand off the floor and reach it overhead.
Press into your left hand and left foot, lifting your hips high.
Arch your back and open your chest toward the ceiling.
Hold for 3-5 breaths, then switch sides.

name: Reclined Pigeon Pose (Supta Kapotasana)
instructions: Lie on your back with both knees bent, feet flat on the floor.
Cross your right ankle over your left knee in a figure-four shape.
Lift your left foot off the floor and draw your left knee toward your chest.
Thread your right hand between your legs and interlace your fingers behind your left thigh.
Gently pull your left knee closer while pressing your right knee away.
Hold for 5-10 breaths, then switch sides.

name: Extended Puppy Pose (Uttana Shishosana)
instructions: Start in a tabletop position.
Walk your hands forward while keeping your hips over your knees.
Lower your chest and forehead toward the floor.
Keep your arms active, pressing through your palms.
Melt your chest toward the floor for a deep shoulder and spine stretch.
Hold for 5-10 breaths.

name: Upward Plank Pose (Purvottanasana)
instructions: Sit in Staff Pose with legs extended and hands behind your hips, fingers pointing forward.
Press into your hands and feet, lifting your hips toward the ceiling.
Straighten your arms and create a straight line from shoulders to feet.
Point your toes and press the soles of your feet toward the floor.
Lift your chest and optionally drop your head back.
Hold for 5-8 breaths.
